domain_description: Classroom talk that actually develops thinking — dialogic moves that extend reasoning, discussion protocols that structure participation, Socratic sequences that go deeper, and argument scaffolds that give students a way to reason out loud. All interventions cross-referenced to peer-reviewed meta-analyses where one exists.

skills.description: Generate specific dialogic moves — revoice, press for reasoning, build on, challenge, invite uptake — that extend student thinking after they respond, so classroom talk does the cognitive work instead of just confirming the right answer.
skills.effect_months_source: EEF Toolkit — Oral language interventions strand
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Dialogic moves require teacher practice — revoicing, pressing for reasoning, and uptake aren't natural defaults for most teachers and need scripted prompts initially. PCK-heavy but no materials, no structural change. Mastery develops over weeks of deliberate use.

skills.description: Pick the right discussion protocol for the purpose — Socratic seminar, fishbowl, Harkness, structured academic controversy, think-pair-share — and configure roles, time, and norms so every student talks for thinking, not just one or two.
skills.effect_months_source: EEF Toolkit — Oral language interventions strand
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Selecting a protocol takes minutes; running one takes 10-30 min of lesson time. No materials beyond a topic and norms sheet. Most protocols are teachable to a class in one orientation lesson.
